title: Natural-language question: critic-guided recovery
why_good: Main live demo path: starts from a real user question, resolves it to the Planner/Critic orchestration code, and returns a multi-commit history about how the agent recovers from thin evidence.
question: How does the agent recover when the first explanation is missing evidence?
talk_track: Shows question mode before history tracing, so the audience sees the resolved target rather than hand-picked line numbers.
Surfaces the Planner/Critic loop as the subject of the answer and as the mechanism running the demo.
Produces several commits and diffs, which makes the final explanation more interesting than a tiny one-commit helper.

title: Config provider switch and env-backed credentials
why_good: Best opening prompt: it has a linked PR, a clear provider switch, and easy-to-explain credentials guardrails.
natural_prompt: Why does config use os.getenv for GROQ_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN instead of requiring API keys at import time?
talk_track: Shows local git history plus GitHub PR enrichment.
Good place to point out cited claims like [commit:...] and [pr:#1].
Connects to the design goal: useful offline behavior without hard-coded credentials.

title: _read_from_revision error-handling history
why_good: Best critic demo: the first explanation is too thin, the critic asks for surrounding file context, and the re-plan visibly improves the final answer.
natural_prompt: Why does _read_from_revision return None when git show fails instead of raising an exception?
talk_track: Shows multiple commits with no PR metadata.
Good place to explain graceful degradation when history is sparse.
The critic loop demonstrates agent behavior beyond one-shot retrieval.

title: Line range slicing bug fix
why_good: Small bug-fix example with a descriptive commit message. Useful as a backup if you need a shorter deterministic run.
natural_prompt: Why did the file context reader need a line range slicing fix?
talk_track: Shows a compact bug-fix trace.
Good backup because the target line range is short and easy to read.
Highlights why line numbers must be carefully handled in history tools.

title: Issue-reference regex extraction
why_good: Good single-commit example for explaining small deterministic tools inside the agent.
natural_prompt: Why does the GitHub issue lookup tool use a regex to extract issue references?
talk_track: Shows a narrow tool with a specific contract.
Good example for discussing controlled tool use instead of arbitrary shell access.
Useful if you want to emphasize testability.

title: Question-mode guardrails
why_good: Good for discussing safety: question mode, line validation, path containment, and public-repo checks all meet here.
natural_prompt: Why does validate_query treat question mode differently from line range mode?
talk_track: Shows input validation before any costly work.
Good for explaining path traversal and span-size guardrails.
Connects the agent behavior to the assignment's safety requirements.

title: Natural-language query: env-backed config
why_good: Best safe natural-language prompt. The resolver can map specific tokens like os.getenv, GROQ_API_KEY, and GITHUB_TOKEN to config.py.
question: Why does config use os.getenv for GROQ_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN instead of requiring API keys at import time?
talk_track: Shows the non-LLM question resolver mapping prose to a concrete span.
Good follow-up after the main demo because it proves users do not need exact line numbers.
Use the resolved_target field to show how the agent grounded the question.

title: Natural-language query: revision reader behavior
why_good: Good question-mode companion to the critic demo. It asks about the same behavior in normal user language.
question: Why does _read_from_revision return None when git show fails instead of raising an exception?
talk_track: Shows that the same investigation can start from a question instead of a line span.
The resolved target previews the code span before history tracing.
Useful if someone asks how natural-language mode works.
